title: The Duck Pond
description: Follow colourful ducks across generations as chance changes the frequencies of their alleles.
detail: Each duck carries two alleles, shown as coloured circles. Explore how random inheritance can make an allele disappear or become the only one left in a population.

title: The Peppered Moth Forest
description: Explore how camouflage and hungry birds change the balance of light and dark moths.
detail: Light and dark moths settle on different tree backgrounds. Birds are more likely to catch conspicuous individuals, changing the frequencies of colour morphs over generations.

title: The Butterfly Islands
description: Follow butterflies between islands and explore how migration changes their genetic composition.
detail: Islands begin with different allele frequencies. Migrating butterflies carry alleles between populations, connecting their evolutionary histories.

title: Island Colonisation
description: Discover how a small founding population can carry a different slice of genetic diversity.
detail: A handful of individuals colonise a new island. Compare the genetic diversity of the founders with their source population, and explore what happens during a bottleneck and subsequent growth.

title: The Butterfly Garden
description: Explore the balance between mutations introducing a colour variant and selection removing it.
detail: New mutations continually introduce a disadvantageous colour variant. Explore how mutation, fitness effects and dominance shape the balance between its introduction and removal.

title: The Chromosome Mixer
description: Mix parental chromosomes and explore how crossing-over reshuffles combinations of alleles.
detail: Two parental chromosomes carry differently coloured genetic segments. Explore how crossing-over creates recombinant chromosomes and can gradually reduce associations between markers, known as linkage disequilibrium.

title: The Recombination Trap
description: Compare chromosome arrangements and explore why inversions can preserve combinations of alleles.
detail: Compare pairing and recombination in standard arrangements and inversion heterozygotes. Explore how an inversion can suppress the recovery of recombinant haplotypes.

title: Tracing Ancestors
description: Follow sampled genetic lineages backwards in time as they meet in shared ancestors.
detail: Begin with sampled gene copies and trace their ancestral lineages backwards until they reach a common ancestor. Explore how population size and demographic history change the pattern of ancestry.

title: Foxes and Rabbits
description: Explore the changing fortunes of rabbits and foxes through their connected population cycles.
detail: Rabbits reproduce and foxes consume them. Follow their populations alongside synchronised graphs to explore how prey availability and predator mortality shape their dynamics.

title: The Food Fight
description: Explore whether two species sharing a limited resource can coexist.
detail: Two species compete for the same limited resource. Explore competitive exclusion, coexistence and the effects of competition within and between species.

title: The Petri Dish
description: Compare rapid population growth with the slowdown caused by limited resources.
detail: A bacterial population expands across a dish. Compare exponential and logistic growth, and explore how a carrying capacity limits continued expansion.

title: Building an Island Community
description: Explore how island size and isolation influence the richness of an island community.
detail: Species arrive from a mainland and occasionally go extinct. Explore how island area, distance and the balance of immigration and extinction influence the number of species present.

title: From Bare Ground to Forest
description: Follow a landscape recovering from disturbance as plant communities change.
detail: Pioneer plants establish on disturbed ground and are gradually joined or replaced by other species. Explore how disturbance, colonisation and environmental conditions influence succession.

title: The Sequencing Zoom
description: Travel from a sequencing instrument to the microscopic features inside its flow cell.
detail: Explore the instrument, flow cell and the regions where sequencing takes place at successive scales. Follow the terminology and sequencing process through labelled layers.

title: Where Does This Read Belong?
description: Find a home for short DNA reads and discover why some alignments are ambiguous.
detail: Align short DNA sequences against a reference genome. Explore how mismatches, insertions, deletions and repetitive regions complicate the search for a read's origin.

title: The DNA Puzzle
description: Piece together sequencing reads and explore the puzzles created by repeated DNA.
detail: Fragment a short genome into sequencing reads, then explore reconstruction through overlapping fragments or a de Bruijn graph. Discover how repeats can create ambiguous assemblies.

title: Finding the SNP
description: Explore how sequencing depth, errors and allele fractions affect confidence in a genotype.
detail: Sequencing reads accumulate at a genomic position. Compare the evidence for different genotypes as depth, error rate, ploidy and the true genotype change.

title: The Molecular Time Machine
description: Explore what fragmented and damaged DNA can tell us about the past.
detail: DNA molecules fragment and accumulate characteristic damage over time. Explore how short fragments, damage, sequencing errors and low coverage complicate the interpretation of historical genomes.

title: Growing the Tree of Life
description: Follow branching lineages as they split, change and sometimes disappear.
detail: Start with a common ancestor and follow lineages as they split, accumulate mutations and occasionally go extinct. Explore the relationships represented by a phylogenetic tree.

title: The Mimicry Game
description: Explore how warning patterns, edible mimics and predator learning interact.
detail: Predators learn to avoid warning patterns associated with unpalatable prey. Explore how the abundance of defended models and edible mimics influences the survival of different colour morphs.
